description: Kaggle competition (2019), real-world card-not-present e-commerce transactions provided by Vesta Corporation, with device/identity features contributed by IEEE Computational Intelligence Society partners.
applicability_notes: No MCC field is published. `ProductCD` (values W/C/R/H/S) is the closest analog to a merchant-category field, but it is a coarse product-type bucket, not a merchant category code, and is not treated as MCC-comparable here.

No official per-customer identifier is published. `card1`/`card2`/`addr1`/`D1` are commonly combined into an unofficial pseudo-customer UID by top competition solutions (widely documented in competition write-ups), but this is a reconstructed heuristic, not ground truth, so it is not used here for a transactions-per-party reference.

TransactionDT is a timedelta in seconds from an unspecified, non-calendar reference point (confirmed on the competition discussion board: first value 86400 = one day in seconds). There is no published calendar epoch, so hour-of-day and day-of-week cannot be derived from the public data without an unverifiable assumption. Not usable as a temporal-pattern reference.
No graph/network structure (party-to-party linkage) is published. Not usable as a graph-degree reference.

n_transactions_train.source: train_transaction.csv row count, widely reported on the competition data tab and in write-ups (e.g. Kaggle discussion #101203).

fraud_rate.source: Competition data tab and near-universally repeated in solution write-ups: ~3.5% positive rate (96.5%/3.5% split).

transaction_amt_shape.value: heavily right-skewed; majority of transactions well under $200, long tail to several thousand USD
transaction_amt_shape.source: Qualitative shape repeatedly observed in public EDA notebooks/kernels for this competition; no single percentile table is published on the dataset card itself, so treat as an approximate qualitative shape, not a precise citation.

time_span_days.source: TransactionDT max value corresponds to day 183 in train (max ~15,811,131 seconds); commonly reported as a ~6-month (182-day) train window, per competition discussion #101203.

usable_for_validation_areas: amount_distribution (overall shape only, scale-invariant comparison -- currency differs from generated INR data)
fraud/background base-rate sanity (not one of the six required areas but noted for context)
not_usable_for: inter_arrival_time (would require the raw per-row TransactionDT values, which are not reproduced here since we do not download the dataset)
